title: Virtual Scroll Container Controller via Imperative Handle
concept: Imperative Scroll Controller with Bounds Clamping
problemStatement: Implement `createVirtualScrollHandle(ref, { totalItems, itemHeight, viewportHeight })` that attaches `scrollToIndex(index)` and `getVisibleRange()` to `ref.current`, clamping indices and calculating visible items accurately.
interviewTrap: Not clamping index bounds causes virtual scroll calculations to display empty white screens.

testCases.name: Scrolls to item index and computes correct offset
testCases.testFn: const ref = {}; createVirtualScrollHandle(ref, { totalItems: 100, itemHeight: 40, viewportHeight: 200 }); return ref.current.scrollToIndex(10);

testCases.name: Calculates visible items range based on viewport height
testCases.testFn: const ref = {}; createVirtualScrollHandle(ref, { totalItems: 100, itemHeight: 40, viewportHeight: 200 }); ref.current.scrollToIndex(10); const range = ref.current.getVisibleRange(); return { startIndex: range.startIndex, endIndex: range.endIndex };

testCases.name: Clamps negative index to 0
testCases.testFn: const ref = {}; createVirtualScrollHandle(ref, { totalItems: 50, itemHeight: 20, viewportHeight: 100 }); return ref.current.scrollToIndex(-5);

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Normally, refs point directly to the underlying DOM node (`<input>`). `useImperativeHandle(ref, () => ({ customMethod }))` customizes the ref instance exposed to the parent component, hiding raw DOM methods and exposing only clean, intentional APIs.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Imperative Scroll Controller with Bounds Clamping.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
